summary: Feed s184_triple is degraded: 18.3% duplicates, 92% encrypted bytes (above 90% NDR tolerance), and required VLAN 20 completely missing (50% untagged). NDR detection coverage is reduced by blind spot on VLAN 20 and inability to inspect payloads.

findings.root_cause: VLAN tags stripped upstream - SPAN/monitor session or packet broker port configured as access/untagged or with VLAN pruning instead of trunk. Results in 50% untagged packets and complete absence of required VLAN 20 that NDR needs.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR is blind to all traffic on VLAN 20, missing half the expected segments. Lateral movement, east-west attacks, and VLAN 20-specific policies will not be detected.

recommended_fix.why: Restore 802.1Q preservation end-to-end: set source TAP/SPAN and packet broker ingress/egress to trunk and forward VLANs 10 and 20 without stripping, so NDR receives complete required VLAN coverage.

findings.root_cause: Overlapping SPAN/mirror sources or dual TAP feeds aggregated without deduplication at the packet broker. Same packets delivered 2-3x causing 406 of 2218 packets (18.3%) duplicates, well above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate flows, inflates session/byte counts, skews analytics and risks false positives or suppressed alerts due to duplicate detection logic.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication (hash-based window) to drop identical packets arriving from overlapping sources within milliseconds, restoring accurate traffic counts without losing unique packets.

findings.root_cause: Feed dominated by TLS-encrypted traffic with no upstream decryption or cleartext mirror. 92% of bytes are encrypted, exceeding NDR's 90% tolerance for payload inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload but receives ciphertext - limited to metadata/flow analysis only. Payload-based detection for C2, exfiltration, exploits is blind on 92% of bytes.

recommended_fix.why: Provide selective TLS decryption/mirror before the NDR (e.g., SSL visibility appliance or key-share) to deliver cleartext copy for inspection while keeping encrypted share below 90% and respecting privacy policy.
